package client

import "testing"

func TestOfflineDisableTruthRequiresSuccessfulKnownReply(t *testing.T) {
	for _, test := range []struct {
		name                 string
		reply                offlineReply
		status, acknowledged bool
	}{
		{"disabled", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "disabled"}, true, true},
		{"ready", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "ready", Enabled: true}, true, false},
		{"staged", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "staged"}, true, false},
		{"capacity-default-false", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "disabled", Error: "client-capacity"}, false, false},
		{"storage-default-false", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "disabled", Error: "storage-failed"}, false, false},
		{"corrupt-storage", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "failed", Error: "corrupt-storage"}, false, false},
		{"failed-without-error", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "failed"}, false, false},
		{"busy-without-error", offlineReply{Supported: true, State: "busy"}, false, false},
		{"unsupported-default-false", offlineReply{State: "disabled"}, false, false},
	} {
		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := offlineDisableReplyConfirmed(test.reply); got != test.status {
				t.Fatalf("confirmed status=%t, want %t", got, test.status)
			}
			if got := offlineDisableAcknowledged(test.reply); got != test.acknowledged {
				t.Fatalf("acknowledged=%t, want %t", got, test.acknowledged)
			}
		})
	}
}
